# v1.0.0

Mitishell is a complete personal desktop shell for Hyprland. It replaces the usual collection of separate bar, notification, control center, on-screen display, and power menu tools with one focused QuickShell setup and one small Go command.

Version 1.0.0 marks the shell's first stable release!

> [!NOTE]  
> Mitishell installs only its own binary, desktop entry, and QML files. It does not edit Hyprland configuration, autostart, caches, user state, or session rules.

## The desktop at a glance

| Workspaces and focused window                                                                                        | Weather, media, and clock                                                                                           | Status and shell actions                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ![The left side of the Mitishell bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aileks/mitishell/v1.0.0/assets/bar_left.png) | ![The center of the Mitishell bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aileks/mitishell/v1.0.0/assets/bar_center.png) | ![The right side of the Mitishell bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aileks/mitishell/v1.0.0/assets/bar_right.png) |

The floating bar is split into configurable left, center, right, and hidden sections. Widgets can be dragged between sections on the bar or arranged in Settings. The default layout keeps frequent status visible and groups temporary controls behind Quick Settings.

![Quick Settings with brightness, Wi-Fi, do-not-disturb, night light, and reminder controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aileks/mitishell/v1.0.0/assets/quick_settings.png)

## One-Shell-Fits-All

The bar shows immediate state and actions. Small popovers handle frequent controls that take seconds. Settings owns complete operational views. Dedicated overlays keep focused jobs such as power confirmation, reminders, and emoji selection out of the way until needed.

![Settings Overview with quick controls, media, weather, CPU, and memory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aileks/mitishell/v1.0.0/assets/settings_overview.png)

### Bar and Popovers

- Workspaces track Hyprland and keep their labels still while the active marker moves.
- The focused window title follows window events and disappears when nothing is focused.
- Media groups duplicate MPRIS players, follows the player that takes over, and exposes compact playback controls.
- Audio, Bluetooth, notifications, updates, weather, clock, system metrics, keyboard layout, tray, and power state can live directly on the bar.
- Quick Settings groups brightness, Wi-Fi, do-not-disturb, night light, and reminders. Audio and Bluetooth retain dedicated widgets.
- The date popover provides a calendar, optional ISO week numbers, and saved secondary time zones.
- Weather is opt-in and provides a three-day forecast from wttr.in with automatic or manual location and locale-aware units.
- The update widget counts official repository and AUR updates. It never installs anything without an explicit action.
- System metrics select a real CPU package sensor when available and report temperature, load average, CPU, memory, and disk state.
- Tray icons open menus drawn with the same Cinder Grove controls as the rest of the shell.

### Settings

Settings has Overview, Audio, Display, Network, Bluetooth, and System pages. Both Settings and the CLI use the same strict config validation. Version 1 configs (from pre-v1.0.0) migrate to version 2 in memory and remain unchanged on disk until the next saved preference.

- Overview combines the controls used most often with now playing, weather, CPU, and memory state.
- Audio manages output and input devices plus application streams.
- Display controls DDC/CI monitor brightness and shows detected monitor state.
- Network toggles Wi-Fi, scans for access points, joins personal and hidden networks, remembers saved links, and reports Ethernet state.
- Bluetooth scans, pairs, confirms passkeys, trusts, connects, and reports battery state when a device exposes it.
- System owns persistent Mitishell preferences, including bar layout, clock format, time zones, calendar week numbers, weather, reduced motion, and notification behavior.

### Notifications

Mitishell is its own notification server. Toasts appear on the correct output, pause while that output is fullscreen or the session is locked, support actions, and move into recent history. Do-not-disturb keeps normal interruptions quiet while critical alerts and fired reminders can still appear.

The newest 50 non-transient notifications survive shell restarts. Captured images and application icons are stored beside the local history. Restored entries stay history-only because their original applications are no longer present to handle actions.

### Audio, Brightness, and OSD

The `mitishell` command changes volume, microphone mute, and DDC/CI brightness through the running shell. Each action shows feedback on the focused output. Rapid brightness changes are combined into fewer writes, and brightness never steps to a value that cannot be reversed from the screen.

Scripts can also show a generic on-screen display with an icon, message, progress value, and duration. Icons can come from bundled aliases, readable local files, the desktop icon theme, Nerd Font glyphs, or plain text. Remote image URLs are rejected.

### Focused Tools

- The emoji picker searches a bundled catalog, supports full keyboard control, copies the selected emoji, and keeps 24 unique recent choices (open with `mitishell emoji` or add a hotkey for the command).
- Reminders use short-lived user systemd timers, can be created from the CLI or overlay, and remain visible and cancellable while active.
- Night-light controls report and switch a user-managed `hyprsunset` process at 4800 K without taking ownership of its service or configuration.
- The power overlay offers lock, log out, suspend, hibernate when supported, reboot, and shut down with confirmation.

![The Mitishell power menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aileks/mitishell/v1.0.0/assets/power_menu.png)

### Multiple Outputs, Access, and Failure Handling

Mitishell creates one bar for every QuickShell screen. Popovers, notifications, overlays, focused-output commands, and screen recovery follow the active output while preserving one shared service state.

Keyboard access, visible focus, readable contrast, reduced motion, overflow, blank states, missing tools, and service errors received shell-wide review. Optional outside tools disappear or report unavailable without taking down unrelated parts of the shell.

## Changes Since v0.9.5

- Replaced separate bar islands with one continuous floating bar and configurable left, center, right, and hidden sections.
- Added drag-and-drop bar arrangement on the bar and in Settings > System.
- Added bounded popovers for Audio, Network, Bluetooth, Display, and Reminders with same-output routing to deeper views.
- Added the default Quick Settings group and compact active-status controls.
- Renamed the main operational surface to Settings, with Overview and System replacing Home and the old settings page.
- Improved focused-window synchronization, Wi-Fi scans, update refresh, media timing, notification placement, multi-output fallback, and system temperature selection.
- Added prebuilt Linux amd64 and arm64 archives, SHA-256 checksums, and bundled third-party license notices.

## Requirements

> [!NOTE]  
> Optional features degrade safely when their tools are absent. Weather is disabled by default because it uses wttr.in. Automatic location allows the service to infer a rough location from the request. Manual location sends the configured place text instead.

- Arch Linux
- Hyprland
- hyprshutdown
- QuickShell 0.3.0
- A Nerd Font for shell and OSD glyphs
- NetworkManager for networking
- BlueZ for Bluetooth
- A working user systemd session for reminders
- `ddcutil` and i2c access for monitor brightness

## Install a Prebuilt Release

Download the archive matching your system and `SHA256SUMS` from this release. Then run:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
tar -xzf mitishell-v1.0.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz    # or mitishell-v1.0.0-linux-arm64.tar.gz
cd mitishell-v1.0.0-linux-amd64
make install-prebuilt
quickshell -n -p ~/.local/share/mitishell/shell
```

## Install From Source

Source builds need Go 1.26 or newer, Qt 6 QML tooling, Node.js, and GNU Make.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aileks/mitishell.git
cd mitishell
git checkout v1.0.0
make check
make install
quickshell -n -p ~/.local/share/mitishell/shell
```
